planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, acidic soil with shelter from cold winds; this Yunnan native is less cold-hardy than Clethra alnifolia and resents root disturbance once established.

directions: This western Chinese relative of the familiar coastal summersweet forms an upright, multi-stemmed shrub with cinnamon-toned exfoliating bark on older wood. In midsummer it produces arching, one-sided racemes of small, fragrant white flowers set against conspicuous dark red calyces and pedicels, a color contrast not found in the more commonly grown American species. Give it a sheltered woodland-edge position out of drying wind, since new growth and flower buds can be damaged by late frost in colder parts of its range. Moist, acidic, well-drained soil and consistent summer watering keep it vigorous and encourage the heaviest bloom.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; like other stewartias it establishes slowly and should not have its root zone disturbed once sited.

directions: Native to central China and still uncommon outside specialist collections, this stewartia species is grown for the same four-season appeal as its better-known relatives: camellia-like white summer flowers with a central boss of yellow stamens, smooth patchwork bark that flakes to reveal gray and cinnamon tones beneath, and reliable orange to red fall foliage color. It forms a small, usually single-stemmed tree that stays in scale with a shaded woodland garden or specimen border. Keep soil consistently moist but never waterlogged, and mulch to protect the shallow root system from summer heat and winter freeze-thaw cycles.
